Neuromorphic computers are designed to mimic the human brain and are particularly excellent at brain-like information processing and learning functions. This makes them suitable for efficiently processing large amounts of data and performing pattern recognition and complex decision-making. They are extremely useful for AI applications, especially in neural network training and deep learning.
OpenAI plans to purchase neuromorphic processing units

OpenAI has signed a contract to purchase $51 million worth of brain-like chips from Rain Neuromorphics, which is developing neuromorphic processing units (NPUs). These chips are designed to mimic the functions of the human brain and are expected to increase computational power in AI training by 100 times and energy efficiency by 10,000 times.

By enabling flexible and efficient computation like the human brain, NPUs can make AI model training faster and more efficient. This is expected to improve the ability of AI systems to solve complex problems and perform more advanced learning and reasoning.

Meanwhile, Microsoft has developed a supercomputer for OpenAI, and this supercomputer runs on Microsoft Azure. This supercomputer was designed for OpenAI to use in training more powerful AI models and to accelerate the development of OpenAI's technology.
